page.text_0083: The text is close but very diverse in genre. Therefore, there are many interpretive perspectives on the text.
page.text_0084: - The first view is that documents are a method of conveying information from one individual to another or from one organization to another through written or electronic language.
page.text_0085: In this view, documents such as permits, notices, reports, questions, documents... are considered documents.
page.text_0086: - Another viewpoint is that documents are papers and documents used in agencies, unions and social organizations. Accordingly, these types of papers are used to administer and manage the activities of agencies and unions or to communicate information to individuals and organizations in society. For example: Decision, Official Directive...
page.text_0087: In general, writing is the form of conveying information in written language. Or it can be understood that a text is a means of recording, storing and communicating information from one subject to another through writing.
page.text_0088: The text consists of a collection of sentences that have content and are closely linked to each other to aim for a certain communication goal.
page.text_0089: To understand specifically what the text is, let's distinguish the types of text that are commonly used today:
page.text_0090: Article 2 of the Law on Promulgation of Legal Documents 2025 defines legal documents as documents containing legal provisions, promulgated in accordance with the competence, form, order and procedures prescribed by this Law.
page.text_0091: Legal norms are general rules of conduct, with general mandatory effect, which are applied repeatedly to agencies, organizations and individuals nationwide or in certain administrative units.
page.text_0092: In case the document contains legal documents but is issued not in accordance with the competence, form, order and procedures specified in the Law on Promulgation of Legal Documents, it is not a legal document.
page.text_0093: The types of legal documents and corresponding promulgating agencies are specified in the Law on Promulgation of Legal Documents as follows:
page.text_0102: Issuing agencies: Standing Committee of the National Assembly, Government, Presidium of the Central Committee of the Vietnam Fatherland Front
page.text_0108: Council of Judges of the Supreme People's Court
page.text_0110: Chief Justice of the Supreme People's Court, Chief Procurator of the Supreme People's Procuracy, Ministers, Heads of ministerial-level agencies
page.text_0115: Administrative documents are the most commonly used documents today, often used to solve cases in the process of state management.
page.text_0116: Administrative documents are divided into two types: separate administrative documents and ordinary administrative documents.
page.text_0117: Special administrative documents are documents showing decisions and directives of state agencies. For example, the Decision on salary increase, the Decision on reward and discipline for cadres and civil servants,etc.
page.text_0118: Ordinary administrative documents are documents that are only informative in nature, for the purpose of operating or implementing legal documents or to solve specific tasks, exchange work...
page.text_0119: Some common administrative documents such as Notices, Dispatches, Reports...
page.text_0120: According to Article 385 of the 2015 Civil Code, "<g id="1">the contract is an agreement between the parties on the establishment, change, or termination of civil rights and obligations</g>."
page.text_0121: The basic types of contracts stipulated in the Civil Code include:
page.text_0122: - Property purchase and sale contract: An agreement between the parties in which the seller will transfer the ownership of the property to the buyer and the buyer must pay the seller (According to Clause 1, Article 430).
page.text_0123: - Property exchange contract: An agreement between the parties in which the parties simultaneously transfer the ownership of the property to each other (According to Clause 1, Article 455).
page.text_0124: - Property donation contract: An agreement between the parties in which the donor transfers and transfers the ownership of his/her property to the recipient without requiring compensation (According to Article 457).
page.text_0125: - Property loan contract: An agreement between the parties in which the lender hands over the property to the borrower; when due, the borrower must return to the lender the property of the same type in accordance with the quality and quantity and only pay interest if agreed or prescribed by law (According to Article 463).
page.text_0127: Property lease contract: An agreement between the parties in which the lessor assigns the property to the lessee for a period of time, the lessee must pay the rent (According to Clause 1, Article 472).
page.text_0128: Contract of contract of leasing property: An agreement between the parties in which the lessor of the contract assigns its property to the lessee of the contract to exploit the utility, enjoy the yield and income and the lessee of the contract is obliged to pay the rent (According to Article 483).
page.text_0129: - Borrowing contract: An agreement between the parties in which the lender hands over the property to the borrower for a period of time without having to pay, when the loan term expires or the borrowing purpose has been achieved, the borrower must return the property (According to Article 494).
page.text_0130: The contract of land use rights means the agreement between the parties that the land user convert, transfer, lease, sublease, donate, mortgage and contribute land use rights as capital or exercise other rights to the other party as prescribed in the Law on land; and the other party shall exercise rights and perform obligations according to the contract to the land user.
page.text_0131: - Cooperation contract: An agreement between individuals and legal entities on the joint contribution of property and effort to perform certain tasks, mutual benefits and responsibilities (According to Article 504).
page.text_0132: Contract for services means an agreement between parties whereby a service provider performs an act for a client which pays a fee for that act.
page.text_0134: Contract for transport of passengers means an agreement between parties whereby a carrier transports passengers and luggage to an agreed destination and the passengers must pay transport fares.
page.text_0135: Contract for transport of property means an agreement between parties whereby a carrier has the obligation to transport property to an agreed destination and to deliver it to the authorized recipient, and the customer has the obligation to pay the freight charges.
page.text_0136: - Processing contract: An agreement between parties in which the processing party performs work to create a product according to the requirements of the ordering party, and the ordering party receives the product and pays the processing fee (According to Article 542).
page.text_0137: Contract for bailment of property means an agreement between parties whereby a bailee accepts the property of a bailor for safekeeping, for return to the bailor upon expiry of the duration of the contract, and the bailor must pay a fee to the bailee, except where the bailment is free of charge.
page.text_0138: - Authorization contract: An agreement between the parties in which the authorized party is obliged to perform the work on behalf of the principal, the principal must only pay remuneration if so agreed or prescribed by law (According to Article 562).
page.text_0139: Invoices are documents used in business activities, purchase and sale of goods and services. Invoices are made by the seller to record the information of selling goods or providing services in accordance with the law.
page.text_0140: A diploma or certificate is a type of document issued to learners after completing a level of education or a certain level of training, course, or refresher program.

page.text_0142: After having an overview of what texts are and what types of texts are commonly used, let's take a closer look at the role and function of texts to see their importance in life.
page.text_0143: - For the State: The document has a particularly important role for a country, which is the factor that legitimizes the behavior of the State government. Without documents, all activities and instructions of the government will have no legal value. The document is proof of the will of the state agency.
page.text_0144: - For other organizations: The document has the role of recording activities, methods of organization and management.
page.text_0145: - For individuals: The document has the role of defining the responsibilities and rights of individuals, and can serve as evidence for the behavior of individuals.
page.text_0147: Every text provides the reader with some information. This is its most important function, because only by providing information to the reader can the other functions of the text be fulfilled.
page.text_0149: This function is unique to administrative documents issued by state agencies. These documents have a legal function, containing legal norms, standards, regulations, and policies promulgated by the State.
page.text_0151: Management functions used in documents for the purpose of planning, building, organizing, building payroll, making decisions... in an agency or organization. This is a powerful tool in the management process.
page.text_0153: This function helps preserve the material and spiritual values ​​created by humans during the process of labor and creativity.
